title: The Brain
core_thesis: The cognitive brain employs high-capacity neural foundation models as unprivileged semantic proposal engines to navigate open-world complexity, while deterministic classical governors retain exclusive execution authority over physical actuators.
pedagogical_strengths: Clear demarcation of the 'Proposal-Permission' principle safely bridges abstract probabilistic deep learning with deterministic physical execution.
Sequencing the cognitive pipeline into five distinct stages (Ingestion to Planning) effectively maps abstract AI concepts directly to chronological system execution.

student_friction_points.point: The introduction jumps straight into dense hardware acronyms (SoC, NPU, HBM) in the image caption before giving the student an intuitive, physical grounding of what the cognitive brain actually does.
The concept of 'action chunking' is introduced without a physical explanation of how discrete token chunks map to continuous trajectory splines or respect joint velocity constraints.
The text mentions 'multi-rate cadence decoupling' but misses an early opportunity to clarify how memory bandwidth and weights-streaming physically bottleneck the 1-5 Hz deliberative inference loop.

established_budgets_and_laws: Real-time physical deadlines and inference latency bounds (deliberative vs. chunking cadences).
Mathematical definition of Softmax (probabilities sum to one mathematically, not as physical truth) necessitating empirical calibration (ECE).
imported_prerequisites: The definition of the causal boundary (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary).
The physical plant of the Body (@sec-body) including strict conservation laws, thermal dissipation limits, and irreversible momentum.
The definition of Physical AI operating 'beyond glass' (@sec-boundary-beyond-glass).
exported_concepts: The Proposal-Permission architecture that serves as the foundation for the Nervous System (@sec-nervous).
Multi-rate cadences (1-5 Hz deliberation vs. 20-50 Hz chunking) which dictate downstream real-time bus scheduling.
Unprivileged neural proposals vs. deterministic safety validation.

surgical_edits.improved_text: The first pillar is open-world semantic generalizability. Classical controllers are geometrically precise but semantically blind: an inverse kinematics solver can expertly drive an end-effector to coordinate $(x, y, z)$, yet it possesses zero understanding of whether that location contains a sturdy mug or a fragile glass.

open_thematic_threads_for_part: How do deterministic real-time fieldbuses safely arbitrate between the stochastic, multi-rate inference of the cognitive Brain and the strict, unforgiving physical deadlines of the Body?
